name: NTRK gene fusions
summary: NTRK1/2/3 fusions are rare in common cancers such as NSCLC and non-secretory breast cancer but are near-defining in secretory breast carcinoma; they predict striking tissue-agnostic responses to TRK inhibitors.
biology: NTRK1, NTRK2 and NTRK3 encode the tropomyosin receptor kinases TRKA, TRKB and TRKC. In-frame fusions retaining the kinase domain with a dimerising partner cause constitutive TRK activation of MAPK, PI3K and PLC-gamma pathways. Secretory carcinoma of the breast characteristically harbours ETV6-NTRK3.
alterations: NTRK3 fusions (ETV6-NTRK3 in secretory breast carcinoma)
Acquired solvent-front (TRKA G595R, TRKC G623R), gatekeeper (TRKA F589L) and xDFG mutations after TRK inhibitors

methods: Pan-TRK immunohistochemistry as screening (requires molecular confirmation)
Fluorescence in situ hybridisation (e.g. ETV6 break-apart)
testing.notes: Pan-TRK IHC is less sensitive for NTRK3 fusions and may be positive due to physiological expression in some tissues. Large NTRK introns can reduce detection by DNA-only panels.

predictiveRelevance: NTRK fusions predict benefit from first-generation TRK inhibitors (larotrectinib, entrectinib) across tumour types; repotrectinib is a next-generation inhibitor with activity against solvent-front resistance mutations.
resistance: On-target solvent-front, gatekeeper and xDFG kinase-domain mutations
Off-target MAPK reactivation (KRAS, BRAF mutations, MET amplification)
cnsConsiderations: Entrectinib and larotrectinib have reported intracranial activity; entrectinib was designed to cross the blood-brain barrier.
